items.tx:
In 2018, I visited Rohingya bastis in Jammu

An intelligence (IB) officer told me he had recorded 1,548 Rohingya families living in the region by then

I asked one Rohingya, 60-year-old Sayed Hussain, how he ended up in faraway Jammu after crossing the border in West Bengal. “I boarded the first train I saw [at Kolkata station]. It was noon. The journey ended at Jammu," he said

Hussain said he was among the first Rohingya to have settled in Jammu’s Bhatindi area 10 years earlier

Another Rohingya, 27-year-old Mohammed Tahir, also gave the same reason

Later, the IB officer laughed at this explanation. Told me, “By all accounts, they boarded the Sealdah Express that crosses Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, and Punjab before reaching Jammu. It’s an arduous two-day journey. Why did they not get down at any of the stations in between?”

There is a syndicate active in Kolkata that has facilitated Rohingya migration to Jammu for years. They tell the Rohingya that the only Muslim-majority state in India is their "natural home"

Ironically, most settle in Hindu-majority Jammu and not Muslim-majority Kashmir. The officer showed me figures on how Rohingya are scattered over 42 sites across Jammu, meaning they are being settled all over the region, and many Army camps were now surrounded by them

In 2015, Abdur Rehman al Arkani, a Jihadi killed by security forces in south Kashmir, was from Rakhine from Myanmar. He went by pseudonym “Chota Burmi”

Role of several Rohingya men in helping Pakistani Jihadis trespass Jammu border had surfaced by then. They are considered experts in infiltration as they are deft in cutting the fence, know tunneling, and are skilled in camouflage. Plus, they have a victimhood narrative of being wronged by qafirs - the Buddhists of Myanmar

In Jammu's Bhatinda are I visited, it was a surprise how quickly they had flourished, as if being pampered and nurtured. An entire lane of shops was called "Burmi market". Most dry fruits factories were employing Rohingya women for cracking walnuts

Local Hindus told me how these infiltrators had bigger and better stocked shops than them, who had lived here for generations

The officer told me how using the UNHCR cards, which have no legal status or validity in India, Rohingya have obtained Aadhaar cards, ration cards and, in some cases, even permanent resident certificate (PRC) cards, all through fraudulent means

Eight years later, these Rohingya are all still there in Jammu. Apparently the govt is running an anti-encroachment drive these days asking them to clear the areas they have illegally occupied, and some of them have reportedly begun to leave

But the exercise is looking more like a temporary inconvenience for the infiltrators than a serious effort to clear Jammu and India of them.

Netanyahu and his allies have beaten the opposition in the Jewish Israeli vote.

That's despite:

- Presiding over October 7th

- Netanyahu being on trial on charges of bribery and fraud

- A cost of living and housing crisis

- Attacks on the judiciary

- Outrage over shielding ultra-Orthodox Jews from conscription

- The Qatargate scandal

- The disastrous Iran war

- The Israeli establishment rationally believing that Netanyahu was making their state a pariah, and organising to get rid of him

- The opposition overwhelmingly also supporting the genocide, occupation and illegal settlements

If we include Ofer Winter's party - which pledged to support Netanyahu for prime minister, but hasn't crossed the threshold - then so far 51.5% of the non-Arab list vote went to the Netanyahu bloc.

With 84.4% of votes counted, among the non-Arab list bloc, the opposition has only increased its share of the vote by about 1.6 points.

Ben-Gvir and Smotrich stood separately this time, but are set to win almost the same combined number of seats as last time.

The latter in alliance with Moshe Feiglin, who declared "Every child, every baby in Gaza is an enemy."

The only significant shift is the surge in support for the Palestinian-led parties.

But most of the opposition is opposed to working with them. Avigdor Lieberman, for example, has taken even more extreme positions towards Palestinians than Netanyahu himself.

If they do a pact with the Palestinian-led parties, not only would it not last long, it would produce a huge right-wing backlash.

That the opposition could on paper form an arithmetical majority with the support of the Palestinian-led parties - but absolutely will not - trashes the "well if the small minority of Palestinians who remained in Israel after the Nakba can vote, then Israel is a democracy for all its citizens" nonsense.

A very likely prospect is that this will pave the way for new elections.

The two right-wing parties which didn't cross the threshold would likely not stand again, boosting Netanyahu.

The same huge mobilisation of Palestinian citizens of Israel would likely not transpire.

Netanyahu and his allies would likely benefit from shock at the unexpected surge in support for the Palestinian-led parties.

The opposition would be demoralised by its failure, and Netanyahu strengthened by having come out on top in this election.

So it's best to bet on Netanyahu winning a coming election.

What does all this mean?

Any illusions that change can happen within Israeli society should long ago have been destroyed.

The opposition would have continued the genocide, the occupation, apartheid and colonisation.

But as Israel's support in the West collapsed, Israel's cheerleaders pushed the position that Netanyahu was the bogeyman, and that a shift in figurehead could allow the state to do a PR relaunch.

Netanyahu isn't Israel, we were told.

Well that's true in the sense that on many key issues, Israeli society is actually more extreme than Netanyahu.

This baseless illusion is now dead and buried.

There must now be a much more determined push for a total arms embargo and sweeping sanctions on Israel.

Those arguing that Israel is something it plainly is not are now completely and utterly discredited.

items.t: 💡MOSSADIL COMMENTARY: THE ARROGANCE OF THE ANTI-BIBI MOVEMENT There is a lesson from this election that goes far beyond Benjamin Netanyahu. For years, a large…
items.tx:
💡MOSSADIL COMMENTARY:
THE ARROGANCE OF THE ANTI-BIBI MOVEMENT

There is a lesson from this election that goes far beyond Benjamin Netanyahu.

For years, a large part of Israel’s opposition has built its political identity around one central objective: Bibi must go.

That may be an effective slogan. It is not a governing philosophy.

You cannot build an entire political movement around opposition to one man, spend an election telling voters primarily who they should reject, and then be surprised when millions of Israelis ask a very basic question:

What exactly are you offering instead?

That is where I believe the arrogance of the anti-Bibi movement became its greatest political weakness.

It operated as though opposition to Netanyahu was itself enough to create a majority. As though the public’s concerns about security, Jewish identity, Iran, Judea & Samaria, the Palestinians and the future character of the state were secondary to the question of Netanyahu’s personality.

But elections have a way of exposing political echo chambers.

The counting is still underway, and the final coalition picture remains unresolved. Early results and exit polls have shown neither major bloc comfortably reaching the 61 seats required to govern on its own.

Whatever the final numbers are, the political choices made after this election may matter almost as much as the results themselves.

Because Netanyahu’s opponents now face a decision that voters will remember.

Do they attempt to build a broad Zionist government with people they profoundly disagree with politically?

Or does removing Netanyahu remain such an overriding objective that they would rather depend on parties outside the Zionist political consensus?

That question became impossible to ignore last night.

At Joint List headquarters, supporters were filmed singing “Biladi, Biladi,” the Palestinian national anthem.

People can interpret that scene however they choose. But politically, opposition leaders should understand exactly how it will be viewed by a very large portion of the Israeli public.

These are Israelis who serve in the IDF, send their children to reserve duty, bury friends and relatives, live through rockets and wars, and may disagree fiercely with Netanyahu.

Many of them are not ideological Likud voters.

Some are centrists. Some are traditional Labor voters. Some desperately want new leadership.

But asking those voters to accept a government whose survival depends on parties whose supporters celebrate an election result by singing the Palestinian national anthem is not a minor political detail.

It is a decision that will have to be defended.

And there is now another issue hanging over the election.

Police arrested three suspects in the Negev on suspicion of attempting to bribe voters to support Ra’am. Investigators say they discovered envelopes containing tens of thousands of shekels in cash and Ra’am ballot slips.

That does not prove that Arab turnout was fraudulent. It does not prove a nationwide conspiracy. It certainly does not justify declaring the election stolen before investigators establish the facts.

But it is serious.

And every credible allegation should be investigated completely, wherever it leads.

What opposition leaders do now will therefore be watched extremely closely.

This is where political wisdom matters.

There are enormous disagreements inside Israel’s Zionist majority. There are people on the center, right and left who disagree about Netanyahu, judicial reform, settlements, religion and state, the war and almost everything else.

But they also share something fundamental: they see the continued existence and security of a Jewish and democratic State of Israel as the starting point of the political conversation.

A responsible political system should be capable of finding cooperation somewhere inside that enormous spectrum.

BREAKING: OBSESSION! Trump derails his own rally to MELT down over President Obama's hilarious Cheesecake Factory joke — proving it got under his skin.

This was a heat-seeking missile from Obama...

"Who could've guessed the joke would've baited Trump into spending the last week of the election talking more about his White House renovations?" observed Jon Favreau, a former Obama speechwriter.

He was replying to a clip from Trump's rally in Mississippi that has since gone viral.

"And now they say, 'Oh whoa, whoa, Barack Obama is gonna start campaigning,'" Trump said in a mocking voice. "And he's not even campaigning— Tell him he's not campaigning about me, maybe he'll go home." 

"But he came in yesterday and he made a speech and part of his speech was to say, isn't it terrible that Donald Trump spends a lot of his time, very little time, I do it very good, I'm really good at real estate and fixing things," Trump continued. "I fix things very good, very beautifully and— I always build beautiful and inexpensive, which is a good combination if you can do."

The truth, of course, is that Trump has zero taste and everything he "renovates" ends up looking gaudy, hideous, and cheap, while simultaneously being insanely expensive because of all the graft and sweetheart deals he bakes in. The estimated cost for his unnecessary White House ballroom has skyrocketed to $600 million, up from the $200 million that was originally predicted.

"But I can do it naturally, it's a natural thing. It actually relaxes me," said Trump, who spends such little time actually working that he shouldn't have any need for relaxation. He's always relaxing.

"'Donald Trump spends a lot of his time fixing up the White House,'" said Trump, in a strange voice. "Isn't that a nice thing to do? The place? No. He said 'this isn't a Cheesecake Factory.'" Can you believe it?"

What Obama actually said was that Trump has the White House looking like "Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory," which is by far the best description we've ever heard for Trump's idiosyncratically tacky preferences.

"Which is a very successful company," Trump went on. 
"This isn't— He doesn't like successful companies. But you know, he was very critical about me because I spend time..." 

Obviously, Obama's point wasn't that there is anything wrong with Cheesecake Factory. His point was that the Oval Office shouldn't look like a place where you can order Roadside Sliders.

"And if you would have seen the White House, I took over the White House and it was in horrible condition," whined Trump. "I don't wanna use a terrible word. It was in horrible condition. The plaster was falling off the exterior, you have an exterior coat...The plaster was falling off. The paint was no good. A lot of the beautiful ornamentation that they have around the windows."

"I mean they had four or five windows where literally the ornamentation was up on one side and had fallen off or half fallen off on the other," he went on, clearly upset. "And I fixed it. We made a mold of the good one and we put it on the other one. And we got it all beautiful. And then we skim coated with an exterior plaster that's phenomenal. The entire exterior with the best artisans you've ever seen. And we delicately one thing after we took a tile that was broken that was. I mean, I don't wanna say from Home Depot, but it does come from a box. And this is not for the White House."

This is what the President of the United States is choosing to devote his energy to with the midterms just one week away and a worsening affordability crisis. Americans are begging for relief from skyrocketing gas prices caused by his disastrous Iran War and Trump is rambling about renovations. Obama really is a master strategist. He lobbed his rhetorical firebomb, then let Trump handle the rest.

Please ❤️ and share if you feel the blue wave coming!

For nearly a decade, the ruling class operated under the arrogant assumption that sovereign power existed solely to protect them and punish you. 

They built an entire industry out of sanctimony, treating the instruments of federal law enforcement as their private political cartel while smiling down from television studios. Look at them today. The mask has slipped completely, revealing an entrenched managerial syndicate trembling at the first genuine taste of their own medicine.

Consider the spectacle unfolding in federal courtrooms across this country. James Comey, the towering figurehead of bureaucratic narcissism who treated the director’s chair at the FBI as his personal pulpit, now sits exposed before the law, trapped under the weight of criminal indictments for unauthorized disclosures and congressional deception. The man who demanded absolute reverence from the public proved incapable of adhering to the basic statutes he spent a career wielding against his enemies.

Beside him in the dock stand the architects of the Foreign Influence Task Force. These ex-FBI officials spent years lecturing the nation about Russian subversion while actively conspiring to bury the Hunter Biden laptop and subsequently lying to congressional investigators under oath. They coordinated suppression campaigns, misled lawmakers, and abused their clearances to safeguard their preferred political dynasty. The stench of their deception is now documented on official criminal dockets.

Turn your gaze to the halls of Congress, where Eric Swalwell remains the living emblem of institutional decay. An elected representative compromised by an operative of the Chinese Communist Party was never expelled or held to account by his party; he was elevated, shielded, and paraded as a defender of national security. The left treats foreign espionage as a minor clerical error whenever the compromised asset votes reliably for the party line.

When you strip away their pompous academic rhetoric, you arrive at their actual objective, articulated clearly by Hakeem Jeffries when he declared this week that ICE will not receive a single dime. The aspiring House Speaker openly announced his intent to paralyze federal immigration enforcement. They demand that American citizens surrender their earnings, obey every administrative diktat, and accept stagnant wages, while criminal cartels and foreign nationals breach sovereign borders with complete impunity. They despise the working citizens who fund this nation, and they intend to disarm the agencies that protect them.

Connect these realities. The weaponization of the intelligence community, the systematic deception of voters, the compromise with foreign adversaries, and the deliberate dismantling of borders are coordinated maneuvers of a predatory elite. For eight years, they believed their control over Washington gave them permanent immunity from consequence.

They are terrified right now because the machinery of justice is finally applying the law without prejudice. The investigators are facing subpoenas; the leakers are facing grand juries; the architects of censorship are running to defense attorneys.

Next Tuesday is an existential reckoning. If you hand Hakeem Jeffries the speaker's gavel, every active probe vanishes overnight. The subpoenas will be incinerated, the criminal referrals will be buried, and the administrative state will resume using the Department of Justice as an attack dog against conservative families, small business owners, and political dissidents.

A vote against the left on Election Day strips the managerial class of their protective umbrella. It drags their corruption into the harsh daylight of courtroom scrutiny. March into the ballot box on Tuesday and deliver the verdict they have spent a decade running from.

items.tx:
ISRAEL ELECTIONS: TURNOUT BY DISTRICT VS. 2022 VOTING BLOCS

With roughly 25 minutes until polls close, here’s the district turnout data as of 8 PM, compared with how each district voted in 2022.

Judea and Samaria: 74.2%, the highest reported turnout. Netanyahu’s bloc received 82.1% here in 2022.

Central: 71.4%, second highest and particularly interesting. Netanyahu’s bloc received 46.2% in 2022, compared with 45.0% for the opposition. Just 1.2 points separated them.

Northern: 69.9%. Arab parties received 38.0% here in 2022, more than either political bloc.

Southern: 67.9%. Netanyahu’s bloc received 58.6% in 2022.

Haifa: 66.5%. The opposition led with 44.1%, followed by Netanyahu’s bloc at 38.8% and Arab parties at 14.7%.

Tel Aviv: 66.0%. The opposition received 52.8%, compared with 43.5% for Netanyahu’s bloc.

Jerusalem: 63.8%, the lowest reported turnout, despite Netanyahu’s bloc receiving 73.8% here in 2022.

The 2 districts with the highest reported turnout are a Netanyahu stronghold and a district where the blocs were almost evenly divided in 2022.

The North, with its substantial Arab electorate, ranks third, while Jerusalem, another major Netanyahu stronghold, ranks last.

Exit polls at 10 PM.

Note: The 2026 district figures come from a locality level dataset with potentially incomplete coverage. They do not reconcile with the reported national turnout of 74.3% at 8 PM and should not be treated as verified districtwide rates.

items.tx:
The Trump administration is considering lifting sanctions on Russia’s sovereign wealth fund, the Russian Direct Investment Fund, according to The New York Times. A U.S. official confirmed the administration is assessing the fund’s application for removal “through established procedures” as part of an effort to “improve U.S.-Russia relations and help end the war.” A final decision has not yet been made.

The Biden administration sanctioned the fund after Russia’s 2022 invasion, calling it a “slush fund” for Putin. People familiar told the Times that Russian officials pushed for relief in talks over the fund’s role in shipping Russian diesel to the U.S., after Trump suspended sanctions on Russian diesel October 9th. Treasury considers the fund already authorized to handle diesel and is running the normal removal process separately.

This would follow earlier actions taken by President Donald J. Trump with respect to Russian sanctions. On October 16th, President Trump signed an order waiving the duties and most of the sanctions provisions of the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act. On October 21st, as envoy Steve Witkoff met with Putin, Russia released Stephen Hubbard, a 74 year old American held since 2022. President Trump wrote that the U.S. “was not required to give anything in return.” In remarks that day he said the U.S. “gave nothing in exchange.” In a Truth Social post just a few minutes later, he wrote that “if sanctions would have been placed, certainly those negotiations would have come to a complete and total halt."

Still only 49% counted.
